newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks off on mild profit-taking - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks off on mild profit-taking - dealers.

text.p: Mexican stocks reversed their uncertain initial gains and were moderately down in early afternoon trade on light profit-taking, dealers said.
"It's a little slow and apathetic, this is. Now we're seeing a small (downward) adjustment, but there could be profit-taking that might continue until Tuesday at least," a floor trader said.
Traders said continued profit-taking was likely after the bourse set three closing records in a row last week.
The leading IPC share index was down 9.22 points, or 0.22 percent, at 4,235.41.
Thin trading volume of 53.8 million shares was inflated by cross trades.
"Dealing has been slack and the day is almost over, the market is very drab," another floor trader said.
Dealers said losses on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones was off 9.95 points to 7,772.09, also weighed on the bourse.
Traders said profit-taking had affected a broad swathe of blue chips, but most notably retail chain Cifra and tortilla and corn flour maker Maseca.
Cifra was off 2 centavos to 13.96 pesos, while Maseca had shed 8 centavos to 8.06 pesos.
Dealers drew attention to strong gains posted by retail chain Controladora Comercial Mexicana, which was up 30 centavos to 6.68 pesos to head the prominent gainers' list.
"I feel a new credit sales scheme announced last week are helping it along," a floor trader said.
"I think it had lagged the market and been ignored. It didn't react until today," a desk trader said, for his part.
On the broad market, of 99 shares traded, 36 were up while 47 were down.
